Action Plan:
1. Urgent clinic assessment today for ongoing fever, night sweats, myalgias and nausea after recent travel; clinician to perform focused history and physical examination to identify a source of infection.
2. Arrange urgent blood tests after clinical assessment: thick and thin blood films for malaria plus inflammatory markers and routine bloods (as documented by clinician). Results to guide further management.
3. Advise the patient not to attend work until evaluation is complete and an infective cause is excluded or managed.
4. If unable to attend central clinic promptly, patient may attend local Emergency Department with clinician’s typed notes; clinician will document suspected tests in the notes to show reception.
5. Administration staff to contact patient to book the clinic appointment; patient to call the number provided in consultation notes after a short wait to be slotted in.
6. Continue symptomatic measures already taken (paracetamol and ibuprofen at recommended OTC doses); no change to current chronic back pain management — continue physiotherapy.
Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 7 days of fever with profuse sweating, intermittent chills, generalized myalgias, nausea with reduced oral intake, and marked fatigue.
- Symptom details: nocturnal sweating; alternating feeling very hot and very cold without clear pattern; nausea persistent all day; mild baseline headaches (longstanding, screen-related) unchanged; no cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, rash, or urinary symptoms.
- Travel history: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; rural exposure with trekking, cycling, time in farmland; took malaria prophylaxis but cannot recall exact medication(s) — reports it was daily and that she “took another one on top of the first one” (details not recalled).
- Past medical history: chronic back pain (attributed to prolonged sitting/poor posture).
- Medications: Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented); over-the-counter paracetamol and ibuprofen (taken at recommended doses).
- Allergies: pollen (hay fever).
- Social history: Nurse by profession; currently working but struggling with fatigue; non-smoker; moderate alcohol intake; moderate exercise several times weekly.
- Family history: father died of myocardial infarction at age ~68.
- Vaccination: reports up to date (including Hepatitis B).

Objective:
- No physical examination findings recorded in transcript.
- No vital signs documented.
- Investigations ordered/planned (to be arranged after assessment): thick and thin blood films for malaria; inflammatory markers and routine blood tests (details to be specified at clinic).

Assessment & Plan:

1. Issue, Problem, or Request 1: Fever with night sweats, myalgias and systemic symptoms post-travel
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Undifferentiated febrile illness (post-travel)
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Malaria (clinician specifically raised concern)
     - Chest infection or throat infection (clinician considered common foci)
     - Other travel-related/exotic infections (clinician noted need to consider)
   - Investigations planned:
     - Urgent thick and thin blood films for malaria
     - Inflammatory markers and routine blood tests (as per clinic’s assessment)
     - Focused clinical examination at clinic to determine urgency and further tests
   - Treatment planned:
     - Symptomatic treatment with paracetamol/ibuprofen (patient already taking OTC doses)
     - Do not attend work until evaluated and cause addressed
   - Relevant referrals:
     - Urgent in-person clinic appointment in central London (admin to arrange)
     - If unable to attend, patient advised to attend local Emergency Department with clinician’s notes

2. Issue, Problem, or Request 2: Chronic back pain
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Chronic mechanical back pain (postural)
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable in transcript
   - Investigations planned: None documented
   - Treatment planned: Continue current physiotherapy and posture/strengthening exercises as advised by physiotherapist
   - Relevant referrals: Under care of physiotherapist (no change)

3. Issue, Problem, or Request 3: Ongoing use of Seroxat / mental health medication
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Ongoing SSRI therapy (Seroxat) — medication noted
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable
   - Investigations planned: None documented
   - Treatment planned: Continue current treatment (no changes documented)
   - Relevant referrals: None documented

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No documented vital signs (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation).
  - No physical examination findings recorded.
  - No specific laboratory/result values available.
  - Exact malaria prophylaxis medication(s) and adherence details not documented.
  - Dose/route/frequency of Seroxat not documented.
  - Exact blood tests beyond “inflammatory markers and routine bloods” not itemized.
  - No documented plan for follow-up after test results.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Patient unable to recall specific malaria prophylaxis; stated it was daily and also described taking “another one on top of the first one” — medication regimen unclear (conflict/uncertainty noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally audible and coherent; occasional short missed words and minor repetitions, but sufficient for clinical extraction.
